items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: I mean you don’t want to go to like performing school and like have somebody like Brittany Spears

ctx.x: You’ve probably played a number of times in well known music schools, universities and so forth. Do you wonder what some of the people that are majoring in jazz now and so forth are going to do when they get out? Knowing what you do about the music business?

Yeah I think it’s tough. I mean it’s always the unusual characters that kind of do the best, the ones that don’t follow the school, that don’t follow the school of thought, that stepped outside of it in some way. And I don’t know how you teach that. I mean I know how you teach somebody, you know you can teach somebody a technical aspect of things and then they have good technique and they have good ability, but I don’t know how you teach creativity or teach somebody to write better tunes or write tunes that’ll…
When you bring a tune to the band, or the other fellows, does it come notated or do you just kind of get together and —
